thesis: Abercrombie disclosed record fiscal-Q2 net sales of $1.3 billion, up 5% year over year, and raised its full-year outlook after continued brand and regional growth. The strongest counter-evidence is that comparable sales were flat and the reported $4.17 GAAP diluted EPS included a $1.75-per-share benefit from an IEEPA tariff refund; that one-time contribution tempers the earnings quality but does not erase the continuing sales growth, increased outlook, and substantial share repurchases. Separately, the federal indictment of former CEO Michael Jeffries and his scheduled late-October trial trigger the fixed governance-history and active-litigation tags, so the operating evidence suggests a long thesis only at low conviction.
invalidation: Comparable sales turn negative across both brands, the tariff-refund benefit fails to translate into durable operating improvement, or management lowers the updated fiscal-2026 sales or earnings outlook.

thesis: Biohaven disclosed a signed global licensing agreement that provides $350 million at closing and another $50 million in 2027, up to $150 million of additional development and regulatory milestones, tiered royalties, and transfer of specified Kv7 obligations to SK Biopharmaceuticals. The strongest counter-evidence is that closing remains subject to antitrust and customary conditions and opakalim's Phase 2/3 outcome remains uncertain; this does not change the read because the signed deal itself supplies substantial non-dilutive capital and shifts future program costs to an experienced epilepsy partner. The active securities complaint has no sourced hearing, ruling, trial, or compliance deadline in the next roughly 90 days, and no qualifying three-year governance event was found, so the evidence suggests a high-conviction long thesis under the fixed rubric.
invalidation: The transaction fails its closing conditions, the near-term cash consideration is materially delayed or reduced, or RISE3 data undermine opakalim's efficacy or tolerability premise.

thesis: KANZHUN disclosed fiscal-Q2 revenue growth of 14.1%, GAAP operating-income growth of 32.6%, 10.8% growth in paid enterprise customers, and 10.4% growth in average monthly active users. The strongest counter-evidence is continuing exposure to China's hiring cycle and platform regulation; that does not change the read because customer, user, revenue, and GAAP operating-income growth all advanced together in the confirmed quarter. Targeted litigation and governance checks found no qualifying scheduled event in the next roughly 90 days and no qualifying restatement, for-cause auditor departure, or operations-related indictment or plea in the last three years, so the results suggest a high-conviction long thesis.
invalidation: Paid-customer or revenue growth decelerates sharply, GAAP operating-income growth reverses, or regulatory changes materially impair the recruitment platform's operation or U.S. listing.

thesis: Semtech disclosed record fiscal-Q2 net sales of $341.9 million, up 33% year over year, GAAP operating margin of 16.3%, adjusted non-GAAP operating margin of 24.4%, and a materially higher adjusted non-GAAP fiscal-Q3 sales and margin outlook. The strongest counter-evidence is that a $101.4 million GAAP tax benefit inflated GAAP net income and GAAP diluted EPS, while the stronger fiscal-Q3 outlook remains forward-looking; this does not change the read because record revenue and expansion in both GAAP and adjusted non-GAAP operating margin demonstrate operating improvement before the tax benefit. Targeted checks found no qualifying fixed litigation or governance tag, so the confirmed operating results suggest a high-conviction long thesis.
invalidation: Bookings and backlog fail to convert into revenue, fiscal-Q3 sales or adjusted non-GAAP operating margin materially miss the disclosed outlook, or AI data-center networking demand contracts sharply.
